```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(mascot) # nolint: undesirable_function_linter.
```

```{r helpers, echo=FALSE}
mood_item <- function(char_id, mood) {
  mascot(
    paste0(char_id, "-mood-", mood),
    character = char_id,
    mood = mood,
    size = 110,
    placement = "inline"
  )
}

mood_row <- function(char_id) {
  moods <- c("idle", "thinking", "happy", "worried", "celebrating")
  htmltools::tags$div(
    class = "mascot-mood-row",
    style = paste(
      "display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 1.25rem;",
      "align-items: flex-start; margin: 1.5rem 0;"
    ),
    lapply(moods, function(mood) mood_item(char_id, mood))
  )
}

appearance_item <- function(char_id, theme_id, label) {
  htmltools::tags$div(
    class = "mascot-gallery-item",
    style = paste(
      "display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center;",
      "width: 96px; text-align: center; margin-bottom: 0.75rem;"
    ),
    mascot(
      paste0(char_id, "-appearance-", theme_id),
      character = char_id,
      mood = "idle",
      size = 84,
      placement = "inline",
      motion = FALSE,
      theme = theme_id
    ),
    htmltools::tags$span(
      style = "font-size: 0.85rem; margin-top: 0.35rem; line-height: 1.2;",
      label
    )
  )
}

to_sentence_case <- function(x) {
  clean <- gsub("_", " ", x)
  paste0(toupper(substr(clean, 1, 1)), substr(clean, 2, nchar(clean)))
}

appearance_gallery <- function(char_id, native_label = "Original") {
  pals <- mascot_palettes(char_id)
  theme_ids <- pals$name
  labels <- vapply(
    theme_ids,
    function(id) {
      if (id %in% c("original", "night_teal", "lilac_violet")) {
        native_label
      } else {
        to_sentence_case(id)
      }
    },
    character(1),
    USE.NAMES = FALSE
  )
  htmltools::tags$div(
    class = "mascot-gallery",
    style = paste(
      "display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 1rem;",
      "align-items: flex-start; margin: 1rem 0;"
    ),
    mapply(
      function(theme_id, label) appearance_item(char_id, theme_id, label),
      theme_ids,
      labels,
      SIMPLIFY = FALSE,
      USE.NAMES = FALSE
    )
  )
}

htmltools::tags$style(
  ".mascot-bubble-region { display: none; } .mascot-gallery-item .mascot-status { display: none; }"
)
```

When you add a mascot to a page, you are choosing who sits beside your reader
and shares the journey. Each of our four characters brings a distinct
personality, five live moods, and a wardrobe of colour appearances to suit the
tone of your screen. Tessa and Sela are settled, while Knurl and Neer are still
finding their final shape.

Here is what a busy afternoon looks like when all four work together.

## Tessa

Meet Tessa, the quiet maker of the group. If you place a mascot without naming
one, Tessa is the friend who steps forward. She belongs to the Hexonians, a
family of characters built on a hexagonal frame who share a couple of friendly
moves like waving and nodding. Her name comes from tessellation, hexagons tiling
a plane without gaps, the way packages fit together cleanly. She began as the
star of a set of short story animations before joining the package as the
default character.

Tessa is innocent and always eager to learn. She is calm, hard-working, curious,
and patient, the maker who thoughtfully picks the right tool and takes the next
step. Where Neer notices what shifted, Tessa builds. You can recognise her by
her slimmer teal hexagon body and the silver ring that shimmers now and then.
She wears hair with a side fringe, a small bow, small studs, hanging arms, and a
chest badge whose icon shows her mood.

Her status lines sound like someone humming along at a sturdy workbench. At
rest, she is "Resting, ready for the next piece." Start a run, and she is
"Working out how the parts fit." If a detail needs fixing, she notes that "One
part needs a closer look." When things go well, she smiles on "That came
together nicely" or "Finished, and built to last." That steady, step-by-step
nature makes her lovely company for tutorials, exploratory tools, teaching
guides, and package documentation.

Here is Tessa across her five moods:

```{r tessa-moods, echo=FALSE}
mood_row("tessa")
```

Tessa wears her own night teal colours by default, but she also comes in nine
other appearances. Here is her full wardrobe:

```{r tessa-appearances, echo=FALSE}
appearance_gallery("tessa", "Night teal")
```

## Sela

If your day involves untangling overlapping appointments, bookings, or shifting
rosters, Sela is the partner you want beside you. She is also one of the
Hexonians, sharing that familiar hexagonal silhouette, yet she brings a very
different rhythm. Sela is the unflappable organiser of the crew, staying calm
under complexity and keeping plans in order.

Her look is instantly reassuring: a lilac hexagon with deep violet hair,
flanked by time blocks that sit apart when things are calm, overlap during a
clash, and slide apart again once sorted. We like to tell a little story about
her name: it is a soft echo of "cell", one hexagon in a grid, and of "selah", the
pause at the end of a line. She hears a clash coming and takes a breath before
fixing it.

Her status updates reflect that composed oversight. When everything lines up,
she announces that "Schedule is balanced and clear." If two bookings collide,
she notes that "Direct schedule clash detected." She takes time "Reviewing
resource conflict," and once cleared, confirms that "Conflict resolved
cleanly" or "All bookings confirmed and locked." Sela makes wonderful company
for appointment managers, booking calendars, and resource schedules.

Here is Sela across her five moods:

```{r sela-moods, echo=FALSE}
mood_row("sela")
```

Sela arrives in her own lilac violet, but she also comes in twelve other
appearances. Here is every appearance in her collection:

```{r sela-appearances, echo=FALSE}
appearance_gallery("sela", "Lilac violet")
```

## Knurl

Some tasks do not call for conversation; they need a diagnostic scan, a clamp,
and a steadfast hand. That is where Knurl comes in. Knurl is a repair robot
belonging to the Visorfolk, a character family whose faces are functional
screens. Deliberate, steadfast, and mechanically minded, it keeps to two or
three words at a time.

Visually, Knurl is built for honest workshop duties: a single-wheeled bot with
a clamp arm and a screen visor. Its name is a nod to a knurl, the
ridged grip pattern cut into metal handles and knobs, a fitting touch for a
repair bot designed to grip tricky problems.

Where the others speak in complete sentences, Knurl keeps to clipped readouts.
When waiting, it shows "Queue idle." Snags bring up "Diagnosing task." A broken
run triggers "Queue error," while a fix brings a brisk "Task repaired." Once
clear, it reports "All jobs finished." Knurl is the right companion for
background queues, batch jobs, pipeline monitors, and diagnostic views.

Here is Knurl running through its five moods:

```{r knurl-moods, echo=FALSE}
mood_row("knurl")
```

Knurl appears in its original colours, but it can also take on four
other appearances. Here is the full set:

```{r knurl-appearances, echo=FALSE}
appearance_gallery("knurl", "Original")
```

## Neer

Neer brings a tranquil, liquid presence to the group. She belongs to the
Elementals family, characters drawn as living elements. Her name means "water"
in Sanskrit and Hindi, as well as in Tamil and other South Indian languages.
Like water, she takes on the colours
of whatever holds her.

Drawn in blue water tones with a shell, Neer is calm, observant, clear, and
welcoming. When something changes on screen, she notices what shifted and says
it in a few words. If something looks amiss, she never panics; worry shows as
attention, not panic.

Her status lines reflect that quiet clarity. When nothing has moved, she shows
"Nothing has changed." As you type, she is "Checking the inputs." Valid entries
give "The form is valid." When values need checking, she flags that "Some fields
need attention," and once everything passes, confirms that "All checks passed."
That makes Neer ideal company for form checks, data entry reviews, and quality
control screens.

Here is Neer displaying her five moods:

```{r neer-moods, echo=FALSE}
mood_row("neer")
```

Neer starts in her original blue water tones, but she can also flow into five
other appearances. Here is how she looks in each one:

```{r neer-appearances, echo=FALSE}
appearance_gallery("neer", "Original")
```

## Pick a companion

Choose the companion that feels right for your page, and let them keep your
readers company.
